sentences.text: In brief, the fact of the case are that the claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation for the death of Late Shri Manoj Rajpoot, who was allegedly involved in an accident while traveling in an Alto car owned by Bhagwan Singh.
According to the claimants, on 14-12-2017, the deceased Manoj was returning from Bhopal, accompanied by Bhagwan Singh in his Alto car.
At around 11:30 PM, the car turned turtle on the Mungaoli- Bahadurpur Road due to rash and negligent driving by Bhagwan Singh, resulting in the death of the deceased.
An FIR was lodged at the Bahadurpur Police Station in District Ashok Nagar, and after investigation, a charge-sheet was filed under Sections 337 and 304-A of the IPC against Bhagwan Singh.
The claimants sought compensation of Rs. 70,00,000/- for the death of the deceased Manoj.

The driver and owner filed a joint reply denying the claim allegations and contended that the vehicle was duly insured with HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Ltd., and therefore, no liability should lie with them.

entities.text: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Insurance Company also denied the claim averments.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:465 3 MA-1845-2022 3.
After hearing the case, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs. 10,85,000/- to the claimants.
The Tribunal found that Bhagwan Singh did not possess a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident, which constituted a breach of the insurance policy terms.

Consequently, the driver and owner of the offending vehicle were held liable to pay the compensation, and the insurance company was directed to pay the amount to the claimants and recover it from the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
4. Shri Bohare, learned counsel for the driver and owner contends that the claimants have failed to prove that the vehicle was being driven by Bhagwan Singh at the time of the accident.
The appellants argue that no eyewitnesses were produced to substantiate the allegations, and the FIR and the final report in the criminal case are not conclusive proof of the accident.
The Claims Tribunal erred in relying on these documents and in holding Bhagwan Singh liable.
It is contended that it was the deceased who was driving the vehicle, and the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is excessive and should be reduced.
5. Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Claims Tribunal failed to properly assess the income of the deceased.
The deceased, being a graduate, worked as a teacher, providing tuition to students, and also ran a hotel.
He used to earn Rs. 24,000 to Rs. 25,000 per month.

The Claims Tribunal incorrectly applied a multiplier of 16 based on the age of the deceased, which was 31 years,
whereas the actual age at the time of the accident was 30 years, as per the deceased's mark sheet.
The correct NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:465 4 MA-1845-2022 multiplier should be 17, as per the guidelines of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017 ACJ 2700) .

Learned counsel for the insurance company contends that the driver and owner of the offending vehicle were in breach of the terms of the insurance policy, as the driver did not hold a valid driving licence.
The insurance company should therefore not be held liable to pay any compensation.
The counsel for the insurance company further submits that the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and appropriate and that no interference is warranted by this Court.
7. After considering the arguments of both parties and reviewing the evidence on record, this Court finds that the driver of the offending vehicle has not been falsely implicated in the case.

It is settled principle of law that if police registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle and after investigation, filed charge-sheet against him, then Claims Tribunal presumes guilty to the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is the duty of the driver of the offending vehicle to enter in the witness box and clear the position that in how and which manner the alleged accident occurred.
It is also the duty of the driver of the offending vehicle to prove that he was not negligent in his part.
In the present case, the driver has not complained anything against the registration of offence to any higher authorities, therefore, his evidence is not reliable.

Thus, the FIR and the charge-sheet filed in the criminal case, along with the circumstances of the accident, provide sufficient evidence to hold that the accident occurred NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:465 5 MA-1845-2022 due to rash and negligent driving.
This Court finds that the deceased was driving the vehicle at the time of the accident is unsupported by any credible evidence.
Therefore, the Claims Tribunal's finding that the driver and owner are liable to pay compensation is upheld.

8. On perusal of record, it is found that according to mark-sheet of deceased, his date of birth is 19-10-1987 and the alleged accident was happened on 14-12-2017, therefore, his age was 30 years two months at the time of accident which is below 31 years.
So, his age is covered in between 27 to 30 years of age and multiplier of 17 shall be applicable.
This Court notes that the Claims Tribunal erred in applying a multiplier of 16 instead of 17.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017 ACJ 2700), the multiplier should be based on the age of the deceased at the time of the accident.

sentences.text:
Since the deceased was 30 years old at the time of the accident, the correct multiplier is 17.
9.

So far as the contention of the claimants in regard to enhancement of compensation amount is concerned, this Court agrees with the claimants' argument that the Claims Tribunal did not award sufficient compensation for loss of future prospects, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses etc.
These heads of compensation are mandated under the guidelines of the Supreme Court and should be accounted for in the total compensation.
In this regard, this Court also observes that the Claims Tribunal had assessed the income of the deceased at a lower amount.
Based on the judgments in Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar (ILR 2014 MP 172), Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways (2008 ACJ 2182), and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi (2008) 3

11. MA No.5217/2022 filed by claimants is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs. 6,71,175/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing the claim petition until its realization.
The said amount should be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The rest of the conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
13. Both the misc. appeals stands disposed of to the extent indicated hereinabove.
